questions.q: What does a Flux `GitRepository` resource actually do?
options: It clones and polls a Git repo at an interval, exposing the result as an artifact other resources can reference
It applies Kubernetes manifests directly to the cluster
It renders a Helm chart's templates
It replaces the need for any kustomize-controller resource entirely
questions.explain: A GitRepository is purely a source: source-controller clones and keeps the repo fresh and exposes it as an artifact, but it doesn't deploy anything by itself — that's a Kustomization's or HelmRelease's job.

questions.q: In a Flux Kustomization resource, what does `sourceRef` do?
options: It sets the container image tag to deploy
It points back at the GitRepository (or other source) that supplies the content to reconcile
It lists the Kubernetes RBAC roles allowed to edit the resource
It names the Helm chart version to install
questions.explain: sourceRef connects a Kustomization to the Source resource (by kind and name) it should pull its content from, which is how Flux links the two separate concerns of 'where config comes from' and 'what to do with it'.

questions.q: What does `prune: true` do on a Flux Kustomization?
options: It deletes resources from the cluster that have been removed from the reconciled path in Git
It shrinks the Git repository's history
It disables polling on the GitRepository source
It converts plain manifests into a Helm chart
questions.explain: prune is Flux's equivalent of ArgoCD's prune option: resources removed from the reconciled Kustomize path get deleted from the cluster on the next reconciliation, instead of being left behind as orphans.

questions.q: What is a Flux `HelmRelease` the declarative equivalent of?
options: A plain Kubernetes Deployment manifest
A GitRepository resource
Manually running `helm install` or `helm upgrade` from the CLI
A Kustomize overlay's patches directory
questions.explain: HelmRelease, managed by Flux's helm-controller, fetches a chart from a HelmRepository and installs/upgrades it using the values committed to Git — the Git-driven version of running helm by hand.

questions.q: Why does Flux split GitOps into separate Source and Kustomization resources instead of one combined object?
options: Because Kubernetes forbids a CRD from having more than two fields
So each reconciliation loop is independent and individually observable, and one source can feed multiple Kustomizations or HelmReleases
Because a single GitRepository can only ever be used by exactly one resource
Because Flux cannot support Helm charts otherwise
questions.explain: Separating the concerns lets one GitRepository feed several Kustomizations or HelmReleases pointed at different paths, and lets each piece be inspected on its own via commands like flux get sources git or flux get kustomizations.
